chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: “O Isḥāq, deal courteously with the hypocrite by your tongue, and devote your sincere affection to the believer. And if a Jew sits with you, then keep good company with him.”

key_terms.بِلِسَانِكَ: with your speech; meaning outward verbal courtesy
key_terms.لِلْمُؤْمِنِ: for the believer; indicating sincere inner loyalty
key_terms.مُجَالَسَتَهُ: his companionship or the manner of sitting and associating with him
key_terms.ٱلْمُنَافِقَ: the hypocrite; one who outwardly shows faith while concealing unbelief

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach Muslims to treat hypocrites, believers, and non-Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches refined social conduct and moral discernment in dealing with different people. It distinguishes between outward courtesy in speech, sincere loyalty to the believer, and good companionship even with those outside the Muslim community.
